note: Art direction for Jiaoren (JR1): after the owner's style reference (2026-09-27), a contemporary Chinese gongbi-style painting of a mermaid on a pale jade-green ground with coral and teal silks. The reference shows a bare-chested figure; only its style is used and every card is fully clothed. Drawn with tools/generate_art.py --reference <the owner's image>.
style: A painting for a collectible card game, in exactly the art style of the reference image: a contemporary Chinese gongbi-inspired painting with fine, delicate ink outlines, soft flat washes of colour, a pale celadon and mint jade-green background with a subtle paper texture, flowing translucent silk ribbons, small silvery-white blossoms and tiny pearls scattered like sparkles, glossy black ink-painted hair in long flowing strands, porcelain skin with rosy cheeks, a calm, dreamy, elegant mood. Palette: pale jade and mint green, coral and salmon pink, turquoise and deep teal, pearl white, with a touch of gold. IMPORTANT: the reference image shows a bare-chested woman in an oval gold frame. Use ONLY its art style, linework, colours and texture. Do NOT copy that woman, her pose, the oval frame or the red seal stamp. Every character is fully and modestly clothed in layered silk robes that cover the chest and shoulders; nothing revealing, kid-friendly, gentle, never scary. One clear main subject, fully in frame. Absolutely no text, letters, Chinese characters, seals, stamps, symbols, logos, borders, card frames or watermarks.

subjects.JR1-H01-kitten: the littlest jiaoren, the cutest of them all: a small girl of about six with round rosy cheeks, huge gentle dark eyes and a sweet happy smile, her black hair in two little buns tied with coral silk ribbons, a short coral silk jacket with a teal collar, and a small plump turquoise tail with a translucent fin. Not a goddess, no crown, no halo. She sits on a smooth rock at the edge of the calm sea, the tip of her tail in the water, laughing so hard that happy tears roll down her cheek, and each tear is a tiny shining pearl; she holds one round pearl up in her cupped palms to show it off, delighted. Tender, captivating, joyful.
subjects.JR1-H01-bigcat: the littlest jiaoren, the cutest of them all: a small girl of about six with round rosy cheeks, huge gentle dark eyes and a sweet happy smile, her black hair in two little buns tied with coral silk ribbons, a short coral silk jacket with a teal collar, and a small plump turquoise tail with a translucent fin. Not a goddess, no crown, no halo. Now she is proud: she rises out of the moonlit sea with her arms raised, a big pale full moon behind her, a necklace of her own pearls around her neck, and dozens of glowing pearls drifting up around her like fireflies, long ribbons of frost-white silk swirling in a spiral around her. Joyful and radiant, still a little girl.
subjects.JR1-D01: a young jiaoren woman with a kind, grateful face, black hair in a loose low knot with a coral pin, in coral and teal silk robes. She has come out of the sea to stay as a guest: she sits on the wooden doorstep of a humble seaside house with a paper window, her turquoise tail curled on the step, folded bolts of pale shimmering silk beside her, and she holds out a white porcelain plate heaped with pearls toward the viewer as a thank-you gift, one pearl tear on her cheek and a warm smile.
subjects.JR1-D02: an older jiaoren weaver with a serene, focused face, grey-streaked black hair in a neat bun with a jade pin, in deep teal silk robes with coral sleeves tied back. Deep under the sea in a quiet hall of pale coral and smooth stone, she sits at a wooden Chinese loom, her long turquoise tail curled beneath her, weaving a length of shimmering frost-white silk; loose silk threads float upward in the water, with small bubbles and a few little fish.
subjects.JR1-D03: no person, an object: a long bolt of shimmering frost-white jiaoren silk, the magic dragon silk, unfurling out of the calm sea in a graceful ribbon that loops up into the air; sea water pours and beads off it and it stays perfectly dry and glowing; a few pearls roll along its folds, and faint pale silver dragon-scale patterns show in the weave.
subjects.JR1-D04: no person: a large pearl oyster lying open on the pale sandy sea floor, a big round glowing pearl inside it, lit by soft beams of full-moon light falling through the water from above, a few small fish and drifting silvery blossoms around it. Calm and magical.
subjects.JR1-D05: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: a cheerful jiaoren boy of about ten with short black hair in a small topknot and a teal silk vest, sitting in a rocky tide pool at the edge of the sea, laughing as a tiny crab climbs his finger, one small shining pearl tear on his cheek.
subjects.JR1-D06: no person: the ice silkworm of Mount Yuanqiao from Chinese legend, a cute, chubby silkworm about seven inches long with a glossy deep-blue-black body, tiny soft horns and small shimmering scales, dusted with frost and snowflakes, sitting on a snowy branch and spinning a long cocoon that shines in five soft colours. Endearing, not creepy.
subjects.JR1-D07: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: three jiaoren children, two girls and a boy, racing a school of little silver and coral fish through arches of pale coral, laughing, their small tails flicking, ribbons of coral silk streaming behind them. Joyful motion.
subjects.JR1-D08: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: a young jiaoren man with a gentle face, long black hair tied back with a teal ribbon, in deep teal and white robes, bowing slightly with his hands together in thanks, moved to tears, and his tears fall as small shining pearls into his open palm.
subjects.JR1-D09: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: a tall, calm jiaoren guardian woman with her black hair in a high knot pinned with coral, holding a long staff tipped with a pearl, floating before the great gate of the Dragon-Silk Palace under the sea, a gate of pale coral and mother-of-pearl, with lengths of frost-white silk hanging inside.
subjects.JR1-D10: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: a kind middle-aged jiaoren healer with a warm smile and a jade hairpin, sleeves tied back, grinding a pearl into shining powder in a small stone mortar, small porcelain bowls of pearl powder beside her, gently tending a little sea turtle with a bandaged flipper.
subjects.JR1-D11: the Muke, the 'wood guests', a hidden folk of the southern Chinese mountains: small spirit people the size of young children, in simple undyed hemp clothes and wide woven leaf hats, with small hooked bird-like claws on their hands and feet. They are spirits, not any real people: seen from behind and half-hidden among tall misty pine trunks, three of them walk quietly away uphill, leaving a neat stack of cut timber under a great old tree beside a small bundle of trade goods; their faces are never seen. Mysterious and gentle.
subjects.JR1-D12: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: a very old, very large and gentle jiaoren grandfather with a long white beard that flows like sea grass, kind eyes, a long silvery-teal tail coiled around a rock in the deep sea, holding a staff of pale coral, dignified and powerful. No crown.
subjects.JR1-D13: no person: a white porcelain plate heaped with glowing round pearls, set on the wooden doorstep of a humble Chinese seaside house by a lattice paper window, a folded bolt of shimmering silk beside it, a few last pearls still rolling onto the plate like tears.
subjects.JR1-D14: no person: the South Sea in a sudden storm, painted in the classic Chinese 'sea and cliff' wave pattern (haishui jiangya) of old silk robes and porcelain: rows of rolling, curling waves in fine ink lines rising around tall jagged rocks, swirling spirals of foam and spray, drifting blossoms flung up into the air, a dark storm cloud drawn as Chinese auspicious cloud scrolls. NOT a single giant Japanese wave and NOT in the style of Hokusai. Dramatic but beautiful.
subjects.JR1-D15: a big pale full moon over a calm night sea, its reflection breaking on the water into hundreds of floating pearls; far away, small, a jiaoren sits on a rock with her tail in the water, looking at the moon. Quiet, wistful and beautiful.
subjects.JR1-D16: no person: folded bolts of frost-white jiaoren silk on a red lacquer tray, the silk glittering with tiny frost crystals like snow, one length unfolding and floating in the air, a few pearls beside it.
subjects.JR1-D17: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: Quanxian, the first of the spring guests: a serene, graceful jiaoren woman with very long black hair and a single pearl hairpin, in flowing white and coral silk, rising from a clear spring that bubbles up from the sea floor, light streaming around her and bubbles like pearls rising. Special and luminous, but no crown or halo.
subjects.JR1-D18: the Muke, the 'wood guests', a hidden folk of the southern Chinese mountains: small spirit people the size of young children, in simple undyed hemp clothes and wide woven leaf hats, with small hooked bird-like claws on their hands and feet. They are spirits, not any real people: one small Muke poet sits on a mossy mountain rock under a big full moon, the wide leaf hat hiding the upper face so only a content smile shows, a wine gourd beside, writing a poem with a brush on a long paper scroll, pine branches overhead. Peaceful and a little whimsical.
subjects.JR1-D19: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: the Loom-Mother, an ancient and kind grandmother jiaoren with silver hair in a high bun threaded with pearls, working a huge, beautifully carved loom in a vast quiet hall deep under the sea, glowing threads of silk rising from the loom like light. The grandest scene of the deck, calm and awe-inspiring.
subjects.JR1-D20: a jiaoren, a sea person of Chinese folklore, with a human upper body and a long, graceful fish tail of turquoise and teal scales ending in a translucent fan-shaped fin, wearing layered Chinese silk robes in coral and teal with fine patterns: a young jiaoren woman at the doorway of a humble seaside house, receiving a steaming bowl of tea from the kind, weathered hands of an old fisherman (only his hands and sleeves visible), smiling, with pearl tears of gratitude rolling down her cheeks.
